title: Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) Simulator — Overview and definition
t: Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) Simulator — Overview and definition
description: Executes and tests PLC programs against virtual I/O without physical controllers.
body: Signature edition. Signature-original methods and framings for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. Executes and tests PLC programs against virtual I/O without physical controllers. A PLC simulator runs IEC 61131-3 control programs with a virtual scan cycle, simulated I/O, timers, and counters, so logic is proven before commissioning. Real implementations include CODESYS Simulation, PLCSIM, and open soft-PLCs like OpenPLC with a simulator mode. It injects faults, records scan-time statistics, and replays I/O traces captured from the plant.
capabilities: Virtual PLC scan cycle with configurable cycle time
Simulated digital/analog I/O with forcing and trending
Timer, counter, and PID function-block emulation
Fault injection: sensor freeze, noise, communication loss
Trace replay from real plant recordings

Teaching ladder for Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) Simulator, simple to complex. Rank 1: name the tool's single core action (Virtual PLC scan cycle with configurable cycle time). Rank 3: run it once on a tiny input and check the output. Rank 5: combine two capabilities: Virtual PLC scan cycle with configurable cycle time and Simulated digital/analog I/O with forcing and trending. Rank 7: chain its output into a neighboring tool (Industrial automation programming environment) with a verification checkpoint. Rank 9+: automate the full workflow and teach it to someone else.
